issue: Each of the three orange GPU boxes in panel B contains an unexplained white rectangle on its left edge and another on its right edge (the red P2P arrows appear to attach to these white boxes). These internal white elements are not defined anywhere: the in-figure legend lists only weights (blue), GPU (orange), data (green), comms (red); the caption ('Each panel names what splits and what communicates') and the grayscale figure note make no mention of them. They are also inconsistent with panels A and C, where the GPU boxes are rendered as solid orange cross-hatched rectangles with no internal white sub-rectangles. A reader cannot tell whether the white boxes mark stage input/output activation buffers, two sub-stages, or the idle-bubble region, which undermines the figure's goal of being immediately interpretable.
evidence: Legend row reads: 'weights (blue) / GPU (orange) / data (green) / comms (red)' — no entry for the white boxes. acceptance_test: Either (a) label the white boxes (e.g., small 'in'/'out' tags) and add one clause to the caption such as 'white boxes mark each stage's input/output activation at the P2P boundary', or (b) delete the white boxes and draw the red P2P arrows directly between the GPU box edges so panel B's GPU rendering matches panels A and C. After the fix, a grayscale reader must be able to state what the internal elements (if any remain) represent without guessing, and the three panels must use a consistent GPU-box convention.
